title: Bambu's Toolchanger Rumor Mill, Prusa Firmware 7.0 & a 15 MB Robot Brain
subtitle: This week in 3D printing news

topics.title: Bambu Toolchanger: What's Real, What's Rumor
topics.description: FCC paperwork and patents say something is coming. A leaked photo this week says nothing at all

slides.heading: Bambu Toolchanger: What's Actually on Record
slides.body: Bambu has announced nothing. Here's the hard evidence, and how old it is.
bullets: FCC filings, Sep 11 to 22: printers labeled H3C, P3C and X2D Pro, plus the S1 scanner and AMS 3H / 3P. Photos sealed until about March 2027
Chinese patents, published Aug 14: a rear rack of 9 printheads plus 1 on the carriage. 10 nozzles, 10 spools in the drawing
It swaps printheads into one moving toolhead. A step past the H2C's Vortek, but not independent tools like a U1 or XL

slides.heading: The "Leaked Photo" and the Numbers Going Around
bullets: Nothing ties the patents to the FCC "H3C" except timing and the letter C
A leaked H3C photo made the rounds Monday. The poster admits AI edited it, and the Bambu forum calls it fake. We're not showing it
Prices and dates floating around ($2,299 H3C, $999 scanner, a mid-October launch) are blogger guesses, not leaks
"March 2027" is when the FCC confidentiality expires, not a launch date
Next real date to watch: Formnext, November 17 to 20

topics.title: Prusa Firmware 7.0: Auto Z-Alignment and HT Hotend Support
topics.description: The CORE One family gets its biggest update in months, and INDX gets 6.9.2

slides.heading: Prusa Firmware 7.0.0 for the CORE One Family
slides.body: Released October 5 for CORE One, One+, One L and One L+. Update before you shim your bed.
bullets: Automatic Z-axis alignment on uneven beds
HT hotend auto-detected, with PPS and PPA presets. Last week's $199.99 400 °C upgrade is now shipping
PVA and BVOH support presets, filament color, tool mapping with Smart mapping

slides.heading: Prusa 7.0: The Fixes, and INDX 6.9.2
bullets: Runout Reaction setting on the CORE One L: act instantly or after a delay
Fixes unreliable homing on CORE One and One+, better nozzle wiper cleaning
CORE One INDX: firmware 6.9.2 on October 7 adds PVA/BVOH presets on the printer
No new State of INDX post since July. PrusaSlicer 3.0 is still at alpha 12

topics.title: A 15 MB AI Brain for a Robot Duck
topics.description: Better Stack fine-tunes Cactus Compute's tiny Needle 3 model to drive a simulated Open Duck Mini

slides.heading: A 15 MB AI Brain for a Robot Duck
slides.body: Better Stack took Needle 3, a model small enough for a microcontroller, and taught it to boss around a simulated Open Duck Mini.

slides.heading: Needle 3: Tiny Local AI That Calls Functions
slides.body: Not a chatbot. It turns a sentence into a function call, and it runs on your own hardware.
bullets: From Cactus Compute, released September 17, Apache-2.0. One set of weights, cut to 2 to 20 layers: 8 to 29 MB
The duck is virtual: Antoine Pirrone's Open Duck Mini running in the MuJoCo physics simulator
Fine-tuned on about 1,700 hand-written examples, 5 to 12 minutes on an RTX 5090. Five tools: walk, turn, dance, shake head, emote

slides.heading: The Duck Learned Manners
bullets: Obeys only if you say please. Gets angry when you're rude. Reacts to "the floor is lava." Ignores impossible asks
49 prompts it never saw: stock 27%, fine-tuned 84%, the 15 MB 4-layer version 61%
Text input only, no voice. The "beats bigger models" claims are Cactus's own
Try it: the duck app is on GitHub, and the written guide walks through the fine-tune

topics.title: A 3D-Printed Filter That Catches Microplastics
topics.description: Researchers print PLA with a sacrificial additive to make pores an FDM nozzle never could

slides.heading: A 3D-Printed Water Filter for Microplastics
slides.body: An FDM nozzle can't print pores small enough to trap microplastics. So the researchers printed the pores in afterward.
bullets: PLA mixed with PEG (polyethylene glycol). The PEG forms tiny spheres inside the print
Soak the part in 80 °C water: the PEG dissolves and leaves a porous mesh
A 20-layer stack removed about 90% of micro- and nanoplastics. Best mix: 10% PEG
Published in Separation and Purification Technology. Reusability still untested
Hackaday's comment thread asks the obvious: does the PLA filter shed plastic of its own?

topics.title: Robotics Corner: The Yeah Hand, a 3D-Printed Robot Hand
topics.description: Five servos, fishing-line tendons and a mostly printed skeleton. Open hardware, kits available

slides.heading: Robotics Corner: The Yeah Hand
slides.body: Vittorio Lumare's open-source, mostly 3D-printed robot hand (formerly Rebelia). Hackaday featured it Monday.

slides.heading: How the Yeah Hand Works
bullets: 5 servos, 15 degrees of freedom. The fingers have no motors: fishing-line tendons run through PTFE tubes to cut friction
Printed in Hyper ABS (skeleton), TPU 95A (fingers and palm) and PLA (covers). STLs plus parametric Blender source
20 kg·cm per finger, lifts up to 8 kg, silicone grip pads and a thumbnail for small objects. 800 open-close cycles without overheating
A flex-sensor glove mirrors your hand for teleoperation. Robotic version has arm flanges and a ROS driver; a prosthetic version is experimental
Licensed CERN-OHL-S (hardware) and GPLv3 (firmware). Kits and assembled hands on Tindie

topics.title: Builder Spotlight: KineticPrints' Moiré Wall Sculpture
topics.description: Two printed discs, one DC motor and nine LEDs make a moving optical illusion for your wall

slides.heading: Builder Spotlight: KineticPrints
slides.body: Rob rebuilt his moiré disc illusion to run on a single DC motor. The electronics got simpler and the effect stayed.

slides.heading: Build Your Own Moiré Disc
bullets: Two fully printed patterned discs. One spins against the other and the interference makes the pattern move. Great under black light
Version 1 used two modified 28BYJ-48 steppers and a custom PCB. Version 2: one brushed DC gear motor on a Pololu MAX14870 driver
Brain: a Seeed XIAO ESP32-C3 or C6 on perfboard, with a ring of 9 WS2812B NeoPixels behind the discs
The board hosts its own Wi-Fi hotspot. Open the phone page, set speed and light effects, and it remembers them
Free files on Printables, firmware on GitHub

topics.title: Quick Tip of the Week
topics.description: Ghost Studio: turn any model into a Halloween ghost in your browser

slides.heading: Quick Tip: Ghost Any Print with Ghost Studio
slides.body: A free web app from a Prusa employee drapes a bedsheet ghost over any model, with the shape still showing through. Let's try it live.
bullets: Drop in an STL, 3MF or OBJ. It loads a Benchy by default so you can see it work in seconds
Export the STL, open it straight in PrusaSlicer, or send it to EasyPrint. No login, nothing to install
Same post, same sale through October 31: Prusament PLA Halloween colors 5+1 free, and last week's Ultraglow + hardened 0.6 mm nozzle bundle 15% off ($119.83)
